evidence: Exists: Connor RJ, Biometrics 43(1):207-211, 1987 (PubMed 3567305). Abstract: 'A simple alternative approximation that is more conservative is presented here.' Discordant-probability dependence not stated in the abstract; full text not opened.
correction: Cite as: Connor (1987) gives a simple, conservative sample-size approximation for paired (matched-pair) proportion tests, improving on Miettinen (1968). Keep the formula (in terms of discordant proportion psi and difference delta) marked [verify] until the full text is checked. Pages are 207-211.

evidence: Field & Welsh, JRSS-B 69(3):369-390, 2007. Summary: 'the theoretical results are limited and more mixed in their conclusions'; 'consistency of variance estimates for a bootstrap method depends on the choice of model'.
correction: Authors: C. A. Field and A. H. Welsh. More precise wording: whether a variance estimate is consistent depends on the model; the cluster bootstrap is consistent under both the transformation and the random-effect models.

evidence: Sec 3.2: 'For 95 out of 357 real faults (27%), none of the triggering tests detected any additional mutants.' Table 4 lists 'Violation of pre/post conditions or invariants (3)'. Sec 3.1: 73% coupled.
correction: Just, Jalali, Inozemtseva, Ernst, Holmes, Fraser, FSE 2014. Invariant violations are only 3 of the 95 faults. The paper also says 17% of real faults are not coupled to any mutants.

evidence: ICSE 2018 abstract (via OpenAlex): 'all correlations between mutation scores and real fault detection are weak when controlling for test suite size.'
correction: Authors: Papadakis, Shin, Yoo, Bae; ICSE 2018, pp. 537-548. The abstract also says higher mutation scores significantly improve fault detection; cite that too, to be fair.

evidence: ICSE 2005 abstract: 'generated mutants are similar to real faults. Mutants appear however to be different from hand-seeded faults that seem to be harder to detect than real faults.'
correction: Authors: Andrews, Briand, Labiche; ICSE 2005, p. 402ff. More precise wording: mutants resemble real faults, while hand-seeded faults are harder to detect than real faults.

evidence: ISSRE 2014 abstract: 'a typical fault involves about three to four tokens, and is seldom equivalent to any traditional mutation operator.'
correction: Authors: Gopinath, Jensen, Groce; ISSRE 2014, pp. 189-200. The finding comes from mining bug-fix changes, not from a fault-detection experiment.

evidence: Abstract: 'Our technique combines test case generation to reveal false positives and mutation testing to reveal false negatives.'
correction: Authors: Gunel Jahangirova, David Clark, Mark Harman; ISSTA 2016.

evidence: Sec 2: 'we systematically reviewed 50 presentations (representing 32 companies)'. Sec 8 (Discussion: Limitations): 'our design does not consider the corruption of service responses, but instead focuses on either the assumed response or a response indicating failure.'
correction: Authors: Meiklejohn, Estrada, Song, Miller, Padhye; SoCC 2021, pp. 388-402. The resulting corpus is 4 industrial microservice applications. The 50-talk review is in Sec. 2, not in the abstract. Text checked against the author PDF at rohan.padhye.org/files/filibuster-socc21.pdf.
